name: Quazeril
description: Quazeril is the most prescribed pharmaceutical in GLMZ, a second-generation GABAergic modulator with SNT-compatible formulation that integrates with BCI wellness monitoring to maintain anxiolytic blood levels automatically. It reduces generalized anxiety, social anxiety, and situational stress responses without the sedation associated with older benzodiazepine-class compounds. Novafold markets it under the tagline 'Perform at peace.'
effects: lowered cortisol and stress hormone cascade
improved social ease and public function
reduced physiological anxiety symptoms — tremor, sweating, elevated heart rate
side_effects: physical and psychological dependence with consistent use
rebound anxiety upon cessation that exceeds pre-treatment baseline
reduced risk perception — users make statistically riskier decisions
sexual dysfunction in approximately 30% of long-term users
BCI integration errors can cause sudden anxiolytic spikes — temporary dissociation
duration: 12 hours standard release; 24-hour extended release formulation available
street_price: Φ 8 per pill (widely available, frequently diverted from prescriptions)
cultural_context: Quazeril is so normalized in GLMZ that not taking it is considered mildly eccentric in Tier 3-4 professional environments. Approximately 61% of the adult Tier 2-4 population has an active Quazeril prescription. On the Shelf, it's obtained through diverted prescriptions or unlicensed generic production. The drug has become a philosophical flashpoint: critics argue GLMZ's chronic anxiety is a rational response to genuine systemic danger, and Quazeril is a chemical tool of social compliance. Proponents call this conspiratorial. The argument is ongoing and largely conducted by people on Quazeril.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 mid-level corporate lawyer realizes she hasn't felt genuine fear in four years — including during situations where fear would have protected her. She wants to taper off but her job performance metrics are tied to her BCI wellness scores, which flag unmedicated anxiety as 'productivity risk.'

The Shelf black market for Quazeril generics is controlled by a single chemist whose formula is reportedly superior to Novafold's branded product. Novafold wants him found — either acquired or silenced.

A city councillor is quietly funding a study proving Quazeril's rebound anxiety rates have been systematically underreported by Novafold. The data has gone missing, and the research team is being pressured to recant.
